Q: Python- %s %f %d % etc A:

Just to add to @A. Gutierrez's answer and provide explanation as to why we do this; In the prior examples (on the site mentioned) we are told that Python "doesn't support mixing operators between numbers and strings."

This solution allows you to overcome this.

For example, you would have noticed that:

if isinstance(myfloat, float) and myfloat == 10.0:
    print("Float: %f" % myfloat)

prints

Float: 10.0

But using the "+ variable" syntax:

if isinstance(myfloat, float) and myfloat == 10.0:
    print("Float: " + myfloat)

Would have thrown the following error:

TypeError: Can't convert 'float' object to str implicitly

Q: What does "=>" mean in import in scala? A:

As others have mentioned, it's an import rename. There is however one further feature that proves astoundingly-useful on occasion that I would like to highlight: If you "rename" to _, the symbol is no longer imported.

This is useful in a few cases. The simplest is that you'd like to do a wildcard import from two packages, but there's a name that's defined in both and you're only interested in one of them:

import java.io.{ File=>_, _ }
import somelibrary._

Now when you reference File, it will unambiguously use the somelibrary.File without having to fully-qualify it.

In that case, you could have also renamed java.io.File to another name to get it out of the way, but sometimes you really do not want a name visible at all. This is the case for packages that contain implicits. If you do not want a particular implicit conversion (e.g. if you'd rather have a compile error) then you have to delete its name completely:

import somelibrary.{RichFile => _, _}
// Files now won't become surprise RichFiles

Update after over a decade has passed since my original answer…

The examples above are for Scala 2, but Scala 3 is now a thing. The Scala 2 syntax still works for now, but in idiomatic Scala 3 you'd write:

import somelibrary.{RichFile as _, *}
// Files now won't become surprise RichFiles

This change is documented in the Scala 3 reference and migration guide.

Q: Calling a helper function in CodeIgniter emits "Call to undefined method" A:

Helpers are the ideal way to declare global functions in codeigniter and what you are doing is correct. Following are just few points that will help you.

  • Load all helpers through single line instead of separate lines.

    $this->load->helper('form');
$this->load->helper('url');
$this->load->helper('login');
    $this->load->helper(array('form','url','login'));

  • If you want to make it global across all the controller files, then you can put it in the autoload.php file located in 'config/' directory. Update the $autoload['helper'] variable as follows:

    $autoload['helper'] = array('url','site');

Source: How to create & call global PHP functions in CodeIgniter

Q: Visual Studio 2026 tab to accept suggested code does not work A:

There is a workaround in this ticket on Visual Studio's website. There was a similar question posted on Reddit, leading to the conclusion that this is not an isolated issue.

Try changing the mapping scheme to Resharper, as stated here: https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Code-Suggestion-could-not-be-used-from-k/11057010#T-N11058693

Nick Albrecht says "I ran into the same issue where it seems like a recent update broke these key bindings. I was able to restore the normal behavior using the keyboard options screen shown above, and using the Reset button near the top right. Be aware this would also wipe any other customizations you might have but I did not have any, and this was faster than making any other changes/corrections manually.

Ctrl-Q (Feature Search dialog)

Search for “Keyboard”

Choose the Keyboard option (not the keyboard shortcut reference)

Optionally change the keyboard mapping to a scheme of your choice, I left it at “Default”

Click “Reset”

Confirm your intent on the resulting prompt, as this will wipe any custom keyboard bindings you may have had." - https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Code-Suggestion-could-not-be-used-from-k/11057010#T-N11058994

Edit 2026-08-08 you may need to restart Visual Studio

Q: Both Java 8 and 17 installed, does java -version always output 17? A:

Check both Path in environmental variable and system variable to the JDK you want to point to, and it should be first and the later one last like JDK 8 if you want than it should be first and than later JDK 17. Make sure you uninstall the recently installed JDK. In my case, I needed JDK 11 and previously I installed JDK 17, so I had to uninstall JDK 17 and then it started pointing to JDK 11.

Change the app pool for the test application from "test" to ".NET 2.0 Apps" as the root of your site has different config from the test application. The windows athentication is setup correctly for ".NET 2.0 Apps" app pool but i think that dosn't effect the "test" app pool.

Q: How does apple create this glass effect in the contacts app of IOS A:

Apple's glass effect (AKA Liquid Glass) is its unified design language and translucent graphic interface used in Apple products and the API document is openly available at:

https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technologyoverviews/liquid-glass

For tooling, start from here:

https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technologyoverviews/tools-and-distribution

Since you are using SwiftUI:

https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/glasseffect(_:in:)

If however you want to write your own code to simulate its effect without using ready-made library, you should know that its rendering algorithms, GPU optimizations, shader code, etc, are all undisclosed as trade secrets.
